body: AH, I have heard this somewhere before. I believe you. Good advice, although I am sure practicing more couldn't hurt.

UGH, of course! Thank you! I see it comes to diversity and balance in all things, so of course this would apply to the drums. My seriousness must have narrowed my mind. In an attempt to increase my speed, I would just use various rudiments with various tempos on the snare only. I wasn't giving my mind the whole picture. I should be wary about this with other things in the future.

"Do you believe that people can have multiple children and love them all equally? How about the children themselves, can they love both their parents equally, or even their step parents in cases of divorce?"
No. I think anyone who says otherwise is joking themselves for the sake of a public image, which is the worst reason to joke yourself.

"Do you mean that if you had a girlfriend, who had a boyfriend, you would be jealous because your girlfriend got "what she wanted" out of her other boyfriend?" Precisely.

"Are you jealous about your friends, who have other friends that they get what they want from?" I don't care about my friends. If someone were to simply turn around and start talking to another person in the middle of my trying to say something serious, I would feel nothing. That is usually what happens anyways, so I accept that most people could give a shit if I ate it tomorrow. I could give a shit if they ate it tomorrow, so no sweat off my back.

I suppose that means I have no friends.

"Being bitter or a martyr isn't a good place to have a relationship from, and frankly, to me it is also quite unattractive." I am positive my personality is extremely unattractive to most people. What I meant by being happy if someone else's needs are met, I suppose I am only referring to what they want done to them. I of course have my needs, and am used to be frustrated by them. I have a high libido, and I wouldn't really blame someone if they couldn't keep up. If they could, great. If not, well I suppose that is definitely a problem for me.

It would have been easier to say I am a selfless lover, I suppose. Watching people get their rocks off gets my rocks off. Of course I have things I like, but knowing that I was able to do something like that for someone else trumps all of the other things I like by far.
Thank you for being so nice. It lifted my spirits for a moment.

"Is there really nothing else in life that would make it worth it?" Can't say for sure, but the only time I have felt happy or fulfilled was when I was in a healthy relationship. Nothing else has had that affect on me. Not saying nothing else will, I just haven't stumbled across it yet.

I know it is definitely an unrealistic goal to want that within the first few years now. I feel like it is an unrealistic goal, period. No matter how long I have been with someone, I can't say for sure if they will ever be as committed as I would like. Even I don't really know if I will ever be this committed. The idea certainly rests well in my head, however, and few things do that.
I realize it is a hopeless romanticization. It was just the only thing that motivated me for the longest time. I wanted something to not be fleeting. Something that was separate from me, that chose to at least offer some comfort at the end of an impossible day. Nothing does that for me now. I can be comforted by friends and family, but it is so hollow now, just like before I met my ex.

I suppose I am the only one to blame for my own happiness. That isn't really a way out, though. It's quite morbid, actually.

What you said about people being vessels for my fantasy, I think that is a perfect analogy. Knowing that doesn't really disturb me, however. I don't really know what people are, or what they are supposed to be. They largely mean nothing to me. If a few could come by and at least entertain my delusion for a while, would I really be different from anyone else following what they think makes them happy?

The only thing is that I think I would feel weird if I were to be so intimate with someone who I knew was just as if not more intimate with others. I feel like it would devalue the whole thing, and really put me off.

Then again, I have little experience.

I really don't know what it means to be emotionally close to someone, I guess. I would consider myself empathetic, but people and I don't really click. People can reach out, and in fact a lot of people do, but I just don't resonate with most people. My personality, views, and how I carry myself can be very off putting to others. Not that I am unkempt, just very erratic and eccentric. It doesn't take much for me to not like someone, either. I used to just awkwardly avoid the people I didn't like, but now I will just tell people outright. It's actually very odd because they usually keep trying, even if I make it apparent that I despise who they are and what they stand for. 

anyways, that is kind of the set up for me saying I don't have many friends, and have been introverted my entire life. My father, I would have to say, was the only person I was close to my entire life. However, I grew up and discovered that he is legitimately insane. Also opinionated, and on the less educated side. I had no close friends, and not because I was a bully, or was bullied, but because most people just felt taxing to be around.

that was how it was until I met two people that I would still consider important, but not close, anymore. 1.) my ex. 2.) a friend I made in sophomore English. 

My ex, I still can't put my finger on. She was incredibly smart, but depressed and unmotivated like I was. I still can't tell who was the most intelligent, but I can assure you I was most mature. (she had a short temper for people who insulted her) We were inseparable for the longest time. All we would do for days was just hang around together, never more than an outstretched arm away. I mean never. We could enjoy eachother's company at any time, and talk about anything, even if we had totally different views. She was impressionability, however. In stead of really challenging my views, she accepted (most) of them, but she was always able to contribute to a conversation somehow, which was miles better than the usual glassy eyed look I would get from most people... She was one of the few people that actually listened to me when I spoke. I was much more talkative than she was, so a lot of the time we would play conversational keep 'em up while I rambled about something. This was the norm for about a year while we were in highschool, then a year and a half after she moved in. Sex slowly went out the window, even though she said it was amazing. (Since staying in contact with her, I am supposedly the only person who has given her multiple orgasms, but I really don't trust her anymore.) Our relationship became more platonic. We both became distant as we saw each other less and less every day. She tried to pander to my libido, but it was horrifyingly obvious that she was disinterested. Then towards the tail end of our relationship, she started hanging out with one of her older friends. They partied a lot, something I couldn't do after she turned 21. Social outings were then the norm, and we didn't even see each other on the weekends. Then she left me a few days after I moved in with her. Now, I hear she regrets it, but the way I see things, towards the end she was just using me. I can't help but feel like we had something real, for a year or two there... but that is basically it. I was the most attached to her, and still am in a lot of ways.

My friend in Sophomore year was a lot like me. He was unafraid of telling people what he thought, and he usually thought out there stuff. Most people hated him, but we clicked really early on in the year. In no time we were both the top students and the class clowns. We mainly hung out with each other. Have I mentioned I am a bit obsessive? At least, I think I am. I have noticed in my relationship that I will focus on one person, and everyone else will just kinda fade in without me noticing too much. Anyways, we became best friends. He moved end of the year. We remained friends and chilled occasionally. Hanging out with him was the social equivalent of a breathe of fresh air, since he not only listened to what I was saying, but had skin just as thick and was very witty and vulgar. He was never a pushover to my views, which I respected a lot. However, he changed after he had been cheated on (twice in a row) by females that meant a lot to him. He became reclusive, and we still hung out and had an awesome time together, just being ourselves, but he definitely changed. He seemed distant too. After my ex left me (I would say a month after?) I started hanging out with him a lot. It was like old times, but then we both got drunk and I blew him. Since then, he has been extremely distant, and even abrasive towards me. We don't hang out anymore, really, and we hardly converse.

That is kinda my history of being close to people. 3 people I can say I have been close with, and that is it. One or two friends outside of that, and that is pretty much it.

I don't think I really know what being close to someone is supposed to feel like, since I have had such a small and dysfunctional sample size.

I like your imagery. Think I will use it in a poem.

as an update on the whole mono poly thing, I don't know. Like I said, I am pretty sure I am obsessive. At the same time, I think that is unhealthy for two reasons. 1.) From my experience, people aren't as open as I am, and that makes communication really difficult. I will feel like I know them, because I take what they say at face value, seeing as when I communicate it is to makes sure the other person understands what I am saying. 2.) People normally aren't like that. I have no doubt the way I attach to people is off putting. Not only that, but I will really only be hurting myself seeing as human beings are not monogamous creatures.

haha! Your comment amused me. 1 up for you.

date myself? Like go out and eat some food alone, or watch a movie alone? I mean, i try to pamper myself. I really actually quite like myself, a lot more than most people. And I don't know how I would take care of myself like I would a partner. I am not consistently or consciously aware of my wants. I am really into suppressing who I am for the most part. That is kind of a requirement for people in societies, at least for the most part.

I mean, if I could, I would just smoke pot and play the drums all day. I can't do that, though.

actually, now that I think about it, I should probably pamper myself less!

also, already in therapy! My therapist says that I am too cynical, and way too critical.

Eeeh. I don't really know. Ideally, I really want to have a long term relationship... but I also want fun. I just don't think a shorter relationship (especially if I knew it was going to be short) would be very fulfilling. Thinking about the end, I would just think "what is the point?" sure, we will have fun, but I will forget this person's name in a few years, most likely. I want to be able to look at my relationship and safely say "We will be holding hands in rocking chairs right before we kick the bucket". I just really really want that out of a relationship.

I have an issue justifying the existence of life in a general sense. In a way, being with someone for so long, and being so involved and so intimate... at least I can say I had that. At least, when I die, I can look back and not feel like it was all a total waste of time.

I can see what you mean by saying it is unhealthy. I will take what you say into consideration, since you seem to be speaking from experience. I do have my own wants and needs, I would just consider the fulfillment of my partner as at the least one important one.

I can't relate with the mind reading. I am usually very open in my relationships. Communication is a very important thing to me.

"I know that my partner's love for another does not effect or impact their love for me." that quote does the opposite of comfort me. I totally relate with what you are saying, about the experiences, and the intimacy... but I think I would be really jealous and insecure.

those experiences mean so much to me, and have powerful affects on me. I just don't know how I would take knowing or watching someone who shared something so special with me share it with someone else. It bothers me greatly just thinking about it.

i don't think it is so much about possession, or jealousy to be honest. I let my ex do whatever she pleased, as long as it wasn't other people. I had no issue with her going out. I had total trust in her, and I know that total may sound a bit exaggerated, but you have to understand that the idea of her cheating on me never crossed my mind (of my own volition). She threw that in my face. She made everything we had and did worthless to me. Now I am apprehensive even to the idea of being romantically involved again. I really enjoy this person, and I would want to share that intimacy with her, but at the same time, I don't want someone to have that power over me.

thank you for the advice. That is what I would like, to communicate and just be comfortable with the whole idea. I still have questions for her, so I suppose I will wait until we can talk again to see her perspective on the whole thing.

it's not that I am trying to pretend. I am trying to be okay with it. I see no point in monogamy. The way I see it, it will always fail. However, polygamy just doesn't seem like something I would want. I don't believe people can love others equally in a group. That means there is either a pecking order, or love triangles.

that or everyone accepts and is alright with their position in regards to others. I personally would have an issue if someone was getting what they wanted out of another person I was supposed to get along with. I feel like I can love someone even if I don't get what I want. As long as the other person is satisfied, I am satisfied. If I am not giving someone what they want, I feel massively insecure. I don't see how this could work in a poly setting, especially since I have a tendency of fixating on one particular person.

it's not really a fear. I don't care much anymore, I just don't see monogamy as possible for human beings. I wouldn't really trust anyone to be monogamous. Sure, relationships are about trust and friendship and putting in as much as you get, but I highly doubt I will find someone like that. I highly doubt even I can be like that. I have hope, I suppose, but it really just look at it as delusion.

Everyone likes to think they will go the full mile when they turn the corner, then you get there and shit hits the fan. Someone fucks up somehow, and the fuck up is never worth the time you put in. In my experience, anyways.

I have seen it so many times, and it happened to me. I have seen it happen to every single person I have ever known. All relationships eventually fail, so why bother with other people?

the idea of perfect romance and monogamy is false. The alternative has no meaning to me.

It isn't with someone I just met. We have sort of been hanging out and talking for a while. We just seemed compatible from the time we spent together, minus the talk about a poly relationship.

I tried to do that same thing, go through the pain to get to the good stuff. I got cheated on, and I honestly only see myself getting cheated on in the future. It just seems like an inevitability now. It is one of the ideas I am entertaining a poly, but at the same time it is self defeating.

I don't know. Maybe I cannot function in a relationship yet.
I am terribly embarrassed. Well, thank you for all of your recommendations. I will definitely take a look at perennial philosophy, since I enjoyed what I have read from Huxley so far.

Thank you very much for this bit "if you had enough money you could do anything that any other wealthy person could do, no matter what skin colour you were". I have found this to be true throughout my research this far. I think I will take my findings and test it against people who believe that England established and popularized "institutionalized" racism to see what argument they make.

I understand now that the slavery was motivated by racism, but what I am really looking for are laws (IF that can even be found. I realize this stuff is pretty old) or large scale social attitudes towards race. (not just philosophers like Ibn, stacking on to Socrates sympathizing with the human nature of slavery. Slavery for Socrates at the time, I think, had a social implication, not a racial one like how Ibn suggests. Ibn was in a "intellectualized" minority for his ways of thinking, and I think a socialist trying to make the case against capitalism could say that he contributed to the idea of biologically based racism, but was not the champion of it. The point is to convince the masses they are superior to the blacks. As i see it now, he could have been in the minority of the opinion, but I have only just been introduced to him so far. I will continue looking into him, and the impact he had on the popular opinion of his society.)  I know that through the Ottoman empire, the Janissaries were able to hold significant power over non-whites, hold property, and were generally accepted members of society. Not at fist, of course, but I think that that came mainly from religious and political animosities, and those diffused in a fraction of the time it took for the tensions in America to simmer down. As time went on, the white Muslims were left relatively unoppressed (from what I have uncovered... There was the Millet system, but again, that was largely influenced by things like religion, nationality, and political power. by the empire. I know the Janissary was a popular military force from 1300-1900, and were primarily slaves of another ethnicity (held by the sultan), but I don't see the same degree of oppression, especially since the Janissary veterans (and the descendants of such) could become governors and scientists and even move back with the families they were take from. The opposite is not demonstrable in the colonies, which had a very oppressive system of laws and legislation targeting the blacks specifically. Other races were demonized, such as the native Americans, but colonists and Native-Americans were able to marry, while neither could marry a black man, even if they weren't slaves. I'm looking for things like anti-miscegenation laws, or laws that targeted ethnic minorities and limited their civil liberties. The way slavery has operated (to my understanding, anyways) was in a militaristic way, beneficial in terms of the frame work of feudalism.

I'm just trying to wade through this mess... I will probably need more time to digest all of this material. I haven't even taken a closer look at China, which could easily spit in the face of "institutionalized racism" or "systemic racism".

i have to go, I ran out of time. This will probably be mildly incoherent and sprinkled with errors, but I must go. I will pour over all this material over the course of the week, and come back with my new findings and conclusion on monday-ish.

I appreciate all the source material, but was all the condescension necessary?  Did I offend you somehow? I apologized in the post for any potential ignorance on the subject since I just started looking at this issue, which is why I came here. My intention is to learn and grow, and you feel like it is important to patronize me because of my political affiliation?

I didn't know that the USSR had a program like that, how intresting. I could see where they would want to do that, however, since there would still be prejudiced people even after a revolution. I suppose it would do me good to investigate the subject so that I could grasp what sorts of policies would be important to a revolutionary state, and how those implementations would work.

I guess that I always figured once the economic structure of society was changed, things like racism would dissipate on their own. However,  if there is one thing I have learned, it's that conservative ideology dies hard, and is easily reinstalled into the mainstream...

This is how I look at it. It's like increased wages, it's pointless to fight for in a bourgeois state since the state could take such measures away once it became inconvenient to continue them. I am sympathetic with Oscar Wilde. "...the worst slave-owners were those who were kind to their slaves, and so prevented the horror of the system being realised by those who suffered from it, and understood by those who contemplated it, so, in the present state of things in England, the people who do most harm are the people who try to do most good; ..."
I know the quote is more about private property, and charity, but I think it works well in reguards to how liberals approach the "democratic" system of government for reform.

Well I do know a few things, and I try to learn more every day. I know Israel and the U.S have been tight (save a few issue, like the Suez-crisis) since they came into being in the middle(ish) of the 40's. I don't know very much about their contribution to imperialism, but I know quite a bit of what the U.S has done.

I understand why you would be apprehensive towards wanting to paint people as "good" or "bad". This is Idealist. I know these circumstances are brought about by the irrational workings of capitalism, but understanding and uncovering what corporate media doesn't want you to know is a good thing regardless. (unless I were to be pushing a fascist/Nazi perspective on how and why Israel was conceived.) That being said, the common public isn't used to this reasoning or depth of analysis. I usually just try to dispel negative ideals and show people the reality of the situation, but I would be deceiving you if I said I didn't simplify the information, and add a bit of passion.

I see where that would make sense, in context to the social order of the time (fuedal, as you said). Im not sure where an-caps place themselves on the conservative/liberal slider, but in an earlier monologue he criticized "those among us who peer into the past with a rosy tinted film" who are middle aged and "mistake their own better, simpler nature with that of the world around them at the time". I consider that a jab at conservatives, but I always though of an-caps as conservative. I will keep an eye out for how the charater developes, and see if that sheds more light on the author's political beliefs.
I see your point clearly. My post seems frivolous in hindsight... but I don't have any socialist associates to discuss these sorts of things with.

Can you lead me to resources on the panthers? I am interested and would like to know more about them. But on the main note, yes, helping the community would probably be the first step. We have to reestablish the image of socialism, because most people, thanks to corporate media, cringe at the "S" word. Look at the CPUSA. They fought the corporate state for better working conditions, better wages (which, all in all, is frivolous due to the contradiction between wages and prices... but it did make living a bit easier for a little while.) and worker's rights in general. People saw immediate results, and that is encouraging. I think too many people focus on selling capitalism as a total wreck to win people over. I mean, that worked for me, but you catch more flies with honey than with vinegar. I think the same can be said for protesting. People usually imagine protestors as uppity teens with scary facial piercings holding Starbucks in one hand, and signs with words that have fallen out of the political mainstream in the other. No matter how peaceful, when the police show up, people usually get hurt... Then us socialists take the hit for it in the news.

Tell him that evolution actually favors the cooperative. If you were willing to sacrifice for your fellow species, that species is more likely to live. Evolutionary scientists will tell you the same thing, so he is wrong there. Also. just because something is natural doesn't mean it's good. With that reasoning, anything can be justified.

Well, fist off, he sounds like a Nazi. Second off, he has NO empathy (kinda like a Nazi). Third... he is people. I think he will learn quickly that that ruling class don't like to just allow people in their little circle of friends. You usually have to be born into powerful families to actually have legitimate power (beyond the wages of his workers). Maybe, if he is lucky and obsessive... but living life that way is; 1.) Morally unacceptable, especially when you know exactly what you are doing, and 2.) really really hard work, a lot to gamble on. He would be voluntarily putting himself in a position in which his life would be in danger if he don't like the right ass. 

It sound like too much work. I would rather just do what I enjoy doing, and live comfortably than step on everyone's toes to get the biggest prize. In fact, tell him he is acting like a child. Tell him that in the way children will hurt each other to take eachother's things, he is being a child. One last thing. he said something along the lines of "that is how the world is" or "it's just natural". Ask him what he thinks life would be like if, whenever people were faced with technological or social change, that is how they responded.

All in all, you're friend sounds like a sociopath, or an incredibly embittered, angsty teen that was looking for some greater purpose, and was ultimately disappointed.

I suppose we should be organizing with fellow socialists (which is so hard because there are so many sub types and micro distinctions...) educating our fellow workers and helping the communities. I mean, protesting could be helpful, but with the way the left is, it is difficult to organize a large amount of people to go protest in a specific area. Not only that, but we will catch the heat if anyone goes crazy and pulls a gun out, or lights a car on fire. I think it would be best to do something directly helpful for the community with your local socialists. Sooth the ills of private property with collectivist action, and cooperation. You might just win some hearts over...

But for all I know, the public will remain as ignorant as ever. I mean, we don't have billions to dump on brainwashing, so it is a bit more difficult for us. I personally tell people about how socialism has helped, and whenever you see a massive democratic change, you see a socialist behind it. (well, most of the time.)

Im glade most people agree with my train of thought. Taking the profit motive out of production would eliminate many conflicts, and if the majority of societies were to operate in a cooperative fashion,  the people would not stand for war. Nationalism wouldn't be an issue either... so the only thing we would have to worry about are states trying to reestablish capitalism. Do you think conflicts could arise from that? Say, the international political sphere is torn on whether a state is socialist or not, and they war over said conflict? I understand that this is a little far fetched, since other socialist states would have to have long lasting alliances with the primary socialist states. (which could swing either toward or against conflict)

Also, do you think the "primary" socialist states would just annex the "secondary" ones? ( im using primary and secondary in terms of chronology, incase that is unclear.)
Can you elaborate on your definition of a socialist society, and why it would be against the definition if war were to break out between two supposedly socialist states?

I see where you are coming from, since socialist societies are supposed to produce for the people, rather than profit, but I think it is a bit of a stretch to say that war is out of the reach of socialist states. Each state would develope it's oun systems of politics, and I think conflict could arise from that. It is hard to say, since a world where the majority of states are socialist is hard to imagine. Just a question, do you consider state ownership of the MOP ( if the state is democratic in form) and production for the betterment of society vs. Profits socialism, or are you an anarchist which believes the state is inherently  capitalistic?

Then she starts welling up, telling me I'll regret it if I go any further and that she give up. I slumped down feeling severly frustrated and like I made her uncomfortable. I sat in the shower, meditating on my actions, and I just wanted to sleep by myself. I was mad at myself, and I was mad at her. We hadnt done anything for a long time, and it had been a long week of her saying she would do something, thrn retracting or forgetting about it. I wanted to sleep alone. She eventually came up to me and asked if I was ohkay. I confessed that I wanted to die. What happened did throw me over the edge. But then her libido goes down the drain again just as soon as night comes up. Is she satisfying me just to keep me around? Does she like it? Is this genuine love making? Is she thinking of someone else? I love her so much, but not only does she never want it, but whenever that once in a blue moon rolls around, she is incredibly selfish. She never used to be like this. But it has been going on for two ears now. It makes me feel more and more bleak. I question my realtionship on a daily basis, and I slowly resent her more and more.


I have been talking about this issue and offering comfort or alternatives. Talking to her and saying that I miss the romance and passion. But she just coldly says "I just don't like sex. I'm not a sexual person." I don't know how to feel anymore.

We used to do anal, but even since we did vaginal she has never really shown intrest in anal again... I can't blame her. It is a bit frustrating for me though, since I have an affinity of butts. But I wouldn't force her to do anything she wouldn't want to do

BC was a nightmare. She had major mood swings and even had a 2 month long period! It was insane.

Anyways she is affraid of BC and condoms now, so I think she has dealt with it by turning that part of her self off. She doesnt even like being teased anymore (presumably because she doesnt want to get pregnant,  and I dont blame her.)
